# Synthetic fixtures

Five KRX packages are committed, all of them under `golden/`, together with
the five text inputs the `create` golden cases read, and they are inventoried
below. Every other archive and document any test reads is built at run
time.

The archive tests need no committed fixture. Every archive they read,
valid and hostile alike, is generated at run time by the test-only synthetic
ZIP writer in `crates/openkrx-core/tests/support/`, which is an independent
original written for this repository and can emit contradictory headers on
purpose. Generating fixtures beats committing them: the intended property of
each archive is visible in the test that builds it, and no opaque binary has
to be trusted or re-derived. A further binary fixture may only be added if a
property genuinely cannot be generated, and must then be recorded below with
its provenance, property under test, and expected result.

## The golden packages

`golden/` is the one documented exception, and it is a matter of timing
rather than of trust: the golden output contract
([docs/testing.md](../../docs/testing.md#golden-output-contract)) compares the
executable's bytes against committed files, so its input has to be the same
bytes on every machine and in every run.

**Provenance for all ten: generated by
`crates/openkrx-core/examples/golden_fixtures.rs`**, in this repository, from
the test-only synthetic writer in `crates/openkrx-core/src/synthetic/`. Every
value is written from scratch here; no clock, no environment and no
randomness reach the bytes, and the ZIP writer stores a zero modification
time, so the generator is idempotent. Nothing is copied from, or derived
from, any real submission or third-party sample, and the supported profile is
KRX-01 in every case. Regenerate them with

```sh
cargo run -p openkrx-core --features synthetic-writer \
    --example golden_fixtures -- tests/fixtures/golden
```

and `python3 scripts/golden.py verify-fixtures` asserts that the committed
files are still exactly what that command produces.

| File | Property under test | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `golden/consistent.krx` | The canonical `KRX/OCD/` layout with a marker, a metadata document and two declared attachments that both resolve to payload entries. | Read and reported; every check passes except `declared_size`, undecided under rule M13, so `validate-structure` exits 4. |
| `golden/no-prefix.krx` | The same package with `Metalayer/` at the archive root, one of the three layouts rule A19 describes. | Read and reported; `root_prefix` undecided under A19 beside M13, so `validate-structure` exits 4. |
| `golden/missing-attachment.krx` | The canonical layout declaring one attachment the archive does not hold. | `attachment_references` fails with `metadata.reference.missing_entry`; `validate-structure` exits 3. |
| `golden/malformed.krx` | The canonical image cut in half, so its end-of-central-directory record is gone. | Refused as `archive.malformed.eocd_missing`, exit 6; nothing is reported. |
| `golden/over-limit.krx` | An archive of 300 entries, above the documented `max_entries` of 256. | Refused as `archive.over_limit.entries` with both numbers, exit 8. |
| `golden/create-manifest.json` | A manifest describing a package with two attachments, one of them renamed inside the package. | `create` writes a four-entry package; `validate-structure` over it exits 4, citing A19 and M13. |
| `golden/create-attachment-a.txt`, `golden/create-attachment-b.txt` | The two attachment files that manifest names, resolved against this directory. | Carried into the package byte for byte. |
| `golden/create-invalid-manifest.json` | A manifest whose attachment object carries `describtion`, a key the schema does not define. | Refused as `manifest.invalid.unknown_field` naming the object, exit 6; nothing is written. |
| `golden/create-missing-attachment.json` | A manifest naming an attachment file that is not in this directory. | Refused as `input.unreadable` with the attachment position, exit 5; nothing is written. |

None of them is asserted to be a conforming KRX package, and neither is the
package `create` writes from the manifest here: essential rules
in [docs/profile.md](../../docs/profile.md) are unresolved, so each fixture is
a shape to observe rather than a verdict.

Future fixtures must be independently authored synthetic originals, never
real submissions or redacted/modified derivatives. Record each fixture's
filename, creator/provenance, supported profile, property under test, and
expected result here. All contributors must have the right to license their
fixture under the accompanying [MIT licence](LICENSE).

Do not copy third-party example packages or schemas into this directory
without separately documented redistribution permission. Never include
personal metadata, real certificate identities, secrets, private keys, or a
complete PEM private-key armour line. Generate keys at runtime if required.

The metadata and profile tests follow the same rule. Every XML document and
every KRX-shaped archive they read is generated at run time by the `meta`
module of `crates/openkrx-core/tests/support/`, from values written from
scratch for this repository.

`crates/openkrx-core/tests/metadata_evidence.rs` deserves explicit note. It
reproduces the *structure* that `docs/profile.md` rules M9 and M10 describe for
the two official `KULDEMENY_META.xml` samples — an XML declaration, the target
namespace bound to an `ns2` prefix, and an attachment reference split across
`ELHELYEZKEDES` and `FAJL_NEV`. It is a **synthetic re-expression of that
structure, not the official sample**: no identifier, description, timestamp,
barcode, note or other text is copied from any primary source, and none may be
added. `docs/profile.md` records that the posta.hu material carries no
redistribution licence. The test is evidence of schema shape only; agreement
with a real service remains unverified.
